# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47 (Bi-Vb Pc47)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc47
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 47. Not relinquishing a communal robe
**Title (English, from literature):** Not relinquishing a communal robe

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 47 (*Āvasathacīvara*) is a gender-specific disciplinary rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the use of a communal menstrual robe (*āvasathacīvara*, literally "communal dwelling robe" or "household cloth") [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. The rule stipulates that a nun who uses the communal robe for two or three nights and washes it on the fourth day must relinquish it to another nun, a probationer (*sikkhamānā*), or a novice (*sāmaṇerī*); continuing to wear it beyond the intended period without giving it up constitutes an expiable offense (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1982; Hüsken 1997; Collett 2014]. Modern scholars observe that while the garment functioned as a hygienic aid, its institutionalization and sharing protocols also prevented individual possessiveness of communal property and conformed to broader ancient Indian and Brahmanical social norms regarding menstrual conduct and seclusion [Sarao and Long 2017; Hüsken 1997; Langenberg, Love, Unknowing, and Female Filth].

Full parallels are preserved in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Bi-Pm Pc 47) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra*, as well as across the Sarvāstivāda and Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya traditions in Chinese and Tibetan translations (such as the Mūlasarvāstivāda *rajaścoda* or *sme gab* rules) [SuttaCentral; Collett 2014; Langenberg, Love, Unknowing, and Female Filth]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 72 texts (247 matching passages), sharing its longest formulaic segments with neighboring rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, primarily Pācittiya 48 (§1.2–2.1.5 ↔ §1.14–2.1.5) and Pācittiya 68, 27, and 81 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the rule with the Tibetan *Vinayasaṃgraha* (D4105) [DharmaNexus]. English translations of the rule have been made by I. B. Horner and Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral; Langenberg, Love, Unknowing, and Female Filth].
